newsitem.title: USA: Ampace sets goal of $40 mln in annual revs.
newsitem.headline: Ampace sets goal of $40 mln in annual revs.

text.p: Ampace Corp said on Tuesday that it had set a goal to reach $40 million in annual revenue by the end of the year.

Ampace recorded first quarter revenue of $7.7 million, a 16 percent increase over the year-ago period. The company also posted a net loss of $138,000 for 1997's first quarter, or $0.04 per share, compared to a net loss of $57,000, or $0.02 per share for the first quarter in 1996.
"We performed better than anticipated and exceeded internal plans for the first quarter, said Bruce Jones, Ampace Corp's chairman and chief financial officer.
He added that the company is focusing on acquisitions and that it expects to acquire more small-to-medium size trucking companies in 1997.

"Achieving sufficient size is the key to our profit objectives for 1997," Jones said. "Our goal is to reach $40 million in annual revenue by the end of the year. This will help rationalize our cost structure and increase our ability to attract larger shipper accounts."
Ampace Corp operates a truckload carrier, MDX, based in Monroe, La., and five short-haul truckload operations.
